subject: garden spider
title: What If a Spider Tried to Spin a Web in Space? In 1973 Two Did

scenes.text: What if a spider spun a web with no up or down? In 1973 NASA found out.
The idea came from a 17-year-old student, Judith Miles. A spider uses its own weight when it builds. So what happens when it weighs nothing?
July 1973. Two garden spiders, Arabella and Anita, launch to the Skylab space station.
Released into a frame, they don't spin. They flail, making what were described as erratic swimming motions.
Then, within about two days, Arabella builds a web. Messy at first. The next ones are far tidier.
One thing gave the missing gravity away. On Earth the silk is the same thickness all the way through. In orbit it came out finer, and uneven. Neither spider survived the 59-day mission.

description:
What if a spider tried to spin a web in weightlessness? In 1973 two of them did, aboard Skylab.
The experiment was proposed by 17-year-old Judith Miles of Lexington, Massachusetts. Two cross spiders, Arabella and Anita, flew on the 59-day Skylab 3 mission that launched on 28 July 1973. After some erratic first attempts they built recognisable webs, but with finer silk of uneven thickness, unlike the uniform silk spun on Earth. Both spiders died during the mission, probably of dehydration, and were preserved for museum display.

first_comment: Spiders flew again to the space station in 2008 and 2011, and after a chaotic start they also managed a tidy web. Which animal should go to space next?
